title: WPSB/202/2014 of Dr. Tej Bahadur Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition B/S( ) . No 2014 of 202
Dr. Tej Bahadur Singh. ........... Petitioner.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. ............. Respondents
Mr. Arvind Vashishta, Senior Advocate assisted by Mrs. Monika Pant, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. U.K. Uniyal, Advocate General with Mr. V.B.S. Negi, Additional Advocate General, Mr.
Subhash Upadhyaya, Chief Standing Counsel and Mr. J.K. Bhatia, Standing Counsel for the
State of Uttarakhand/respondent nos.1 & 2.
Mr. Aman Rab, Advocate for the respondent nos.3 & 4.
JUDGMENT
Coram: Hon'ble K.M. Joseph, C.J.
 Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Dated: 9th September, 2014
K.M. JOSEPH, C.J. (Oral)
 Petitioner was appointed as a Scientific Officer in the year 1991 in
the Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board. He became a Senior
Scientific Officer in the year 2002. In the year 2005, he was appointed on
deputation as Chief Environmental Officer in the Uttaranchal
Environment Protection and Pollution Control Board vide Annexure No.4
for a period of three years. According to the petitioner, he performed well
and completed the tenure. In the year 2011, according to the petitioner, he
came to know that one post of Chief Environmental Officer is vacant in
the State of Uttarakhand. According to the petitioner, his family is settled
down in Dehradun. He, accordingly, moved an application with his Bio-data before the Member Secretary. He also obtained Annexure -8 No
Objection Certificate from the Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control
Board. Further averment in the writ petition is that the Government of
Uttarakhand agreed to appoint the petitioner on deputation to the post of
Chief Environmental Officer and that the Additional Secretary in the
Government of Uttarakhand appointed him on deputation vide Annexure
No.9 dated 10.09.2013. It is his further case that he submitted a joining
report, as sought to be established through Annexure Nos. 12 & 13 dated

2
16.09.2013. It is, thereupon, according to him, that he came to know of
the impugned order in this case dated 17.09.2013 issued by the Additional
Secretary, Government of Uttarakhand (second respondent), whereunder
the order dated 10.09.2013, referred to hereinbefore, was ordered to be
kept in abeyance. According to him, he had made applications for
revoking the suspension order. Being unsuccessful, he approached this
Court by filing the present writ petition on 01.07.2014.
2. When the matter came up upon 03.07.2014, this Court was
persuaded to stay the impugned order dated 17.09.2013 till further orders
and he obtained the further order, by which the respondents were directed
to permit him to work provisionally on the post he was given appointment
vide letter dated 10.09.2013.
3. Counter affidavits have been filed by the contesting respondents.
They have taken the stand essentially that the Uttarakhand Environment
Protection and Pollution Control Board was constituted in the year 2002
under The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
(hereinafter referred to as the "Water Act"). As per the same, the Rules,
which have been framed in the Uttar Pradesh out of which State of
Uttarakhand is carved out, provide for appointment to the post of
Environmental Officer by way of promotion. It is also the case that there
is no order of appointment by the competent person, namely, the
Chairman. There is also a reference to complaints, which were received
against the petitioner when he was previously working as the
Environmental Officer. These complaints were investigated and an
enquiry was conducted.
4. A Rejoinder affidavit has also been filed.
5. We have heard Mr. Arvind Vashishth the learned Senior Counsel
for the petitioner, Mr. U.K. Uniyal, learned Advocate General for the
State and also Mr. Aman Rab, Advocate appearing on behalf of
respondent nos. 3 & 4.

3
6. Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner would point out the facts
and submits that orders have been issued and they are justifiable on the
following basis. He would submit that the Water Act was enacted in the
year 1974. He invited our attention to the fact that Section 1 would show
that various States had agreed apparently for the Act being made by the
Parliament and it would apply to any of the State, which would adopt it
under Article 252. He, therefore, would pose a question as to whether the
Water Act has been adopted by the State of Uttarakhand as provided in
the Constitution? Next, he would draw our attention towards Section 12
of the Water Act and he would submit that, thereunder, the Board has to
appoint such officers subject to Rules as may be framed in the case of the
State Board by the State Government. Thereafter, he draws our attention
to Sub-Section (3-A) of Section 12 of the Water Act, which reads as
follows:
"[(3A) The method of recruitment and the terms and conditions of
service (including the scales of pay) of the officers (other than the
member-secretary) and other employees of the Central Board or a
State Board shall be such as may be determined by regulations made
by the Central Board or, as the case may be, by the State Board:
Provided that no regulation made under this sub-section shall
take effect unless, -
(a) in the case of a regulation made by the Central Board, it is
approved by the Central Government; and
(b) in the case of a regulation made by a State Board, it is approved
by the State Government.]"
7. Next, he would immediately invite our attention to The Air
(Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 (hereinafter referred to as
the Air Act). Thereunder, he would draw our attention to Section 14.
Section 14 reads as follows:
 "14. Member-secretary and officers and other employees of
State Boards.-(1) The terms and conditions of service of the
member-secretary of a State Board constituted under this Act shall
be such as may be prescribed.
 [(2) The member-secretary of a State Board, whether constituted
under this Act or not, shall exercise such powers and perform such
duties as may be prescribed, or as may, from time to time, be
delegated to him by the State Board or its Chairman.]
 (3) Subject to such rules as may be made by the State
Government in this behalf, a State Board, whether constituted under

4
this Act or not, may appoint such officers and other employees as it
considers necessary for the efficient performance of its functions
under this Act.
 (4) The method of appointment, the conditions of service and the
scales of pay of the officers (other than the member-secretary) and
other employees of a State Board appointed under sub-section (3)
shall be such as may be determined by regulations made by the
State Board under this Act.
 (5) Subject to such conditions as may be prescribed, a State
Board constituted under this Act may, from time to time appoint
any qualified person to be a consultant to the Board and pay him
such salary and allowances or fees, as it thinks fit."
8. He would contrast the nature of the power enjoyed by the Board
under the respective Acts and he would contend that there is difference in
the power of the Board to make Regulations. Whereas in the Water Act,
the power of the Board is made dependent on approval granted by the
State Government, there is no such requirement in regard to Regulations
made by the Board under Section 14 (4) of the later enactment in the Act.
Therefore, the principle that the later enactment must prevail, learned
Senior Counsel would contend that it is open to the Board to make
Regulations immediately. He drew our attention to Section 21 of the
General Clauses Act, which reads as follows:
"21. Power to make to include power to add to, amend, vary or
rescind [statutory instruments]. -Where, by any [Uttar Pradesh]
Act, a power to issue [statutory instruments] is conferred, then that
power includes a power, exercisable in the like manner and subject
to the like sanction and conditions (if any), to add, amend, vary, or
rescind any [statutory instruments] so issued."
9. He also drew our attention to an unreported judgment of the
Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Rajasthan and others Vs.
M/s Basant Agrotech (India) Ltd. and others, decided on 06.12.2013.
10. His contention, in short, is that it is open to amend or vary
Regulation and such a varying or amendment of the so called 1995 Rules,
which are relied upon by the respondents, took place when a resolution
was passed by the Board on 04.11.2003, wherein the Board, inter alia, on
04.11.2003, which is the second Board Resolution, took the following
decision:
12. Recruitment of Boards Board has granted approval for filling

5
vacant posts vacant posts by deputation / direct
recruitment. It was also decided
appointments may be made in
accordance with qualification as
prescribed the U.P. Pollution Control
Board service regulation. It was also
resolved / decided that Uttaranchal
service regulation may be drafted
before next Board meeting.

11. Therefore, he would contend that this amounts to making of a
Regulation or varying of the earlier Regulation, even if it is applicable to
the State of Uttaranchal. He would immediately draw our attention also
to Regulations, which, according to him, have been made by the
Uttaranchal Board in the year 2006, as per which, for the post of Chief
Environmental Officer, the mode of recruitment is shown as the direct
recruitment or deputation or promotion and the Appointing Authority
remains the same i.e. the Chairperson as is mentioned in the 1995
Regulations. Therefore, he would submit that, insofar under the Air Act,
there is no requirement that there should be approval of the State
Government; the Regulations have come into force on their own and,
therefore, the appointment of the petitioner by way of deputation cannot
be frowned upon with reference to Regulations, which were extant in the
State of Uttar Pradesh and allegedly made applicable in the State of
Uttarakhand. He would further point out that with reference to the
Notings in the Government File (to be found at page 441 of the paper
book), the Chairperson has indeed made the appointment. According to
him, the Chairperson is none other, but the Principal Secretary,
Government of Uttarakhand, Ministry of Environment and Forest. The
following is the Noting, which is referred to:

As directed by the Hon. Chief Minister, a note regarding the
background of the issue related to posting of Shri T.B. Singh
on deputation to the post of Chief Environmental Officer,
Uttarakhand Environment Protection and Pollution Control
Board is put up in pages 98-100 ante for your kind perusal.

6
Hon. Chief Minister had instructed to appoint Shri T.B.
Singh as CEO, UEPCCB for a period on one year on
deputation.
May like to give necessary instructions please.

Sd/-
 (S.Ramaswamy)
 Principal Secretary
 6/9
Hon.Chief Minister

Sd/. (Illegible)
 6/9"
12. He draws our attention to the further noting dated 06.09.2013. He
would thereafter point out that the order is there and signed by the very
same Sri S. Ramaswamy, the Principal Secretary or the Chairperson,
which reads as follows:
"Issue orders as conveyed by the C.M. for one year period. Put up
file for Hon'ble C.M.'s ... (as the words are not clear to us) with
compliance report."
13. Thereafter, he would contend that there is an order by the
Chairperson, who is indeed the Appointing Authority. He would further
submit that the petitioner is not to blame as it is the Authority, who
decided to appoint him.
14. Per contra, the learned Advocate General would contend that here
is the case, where the petitioner has come to this Court on the basis of a
plea, which is itself founded on an order of an Authority, here the
Additional Secretary of the Government, who is not the Appointing
Authority. Even assuming that everything that is argued by the petitioner
is correct, still there is no order by the competent Authority, namely, the
Chairperson, by which he stands appointed. He read out the order dated
10.09.2013, which is the sheet anchor of the petitioner and pointed out
that the order was issued by the Additional Secretary. On the short
ground, he would submit that the petitioner must be non-suited. He
would, in fact, submit that there is no authority for the Government at all

7
in this matter and it was realizing this mistake that it was noted in the next
page at Page 443 that the earlier order may be kept in abeyance. That
order is dated 16.09.2013 and that led to issuance of the impugned order
dated 17.09.2013.
15. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Board would point out
that the petitioner has approached this Court with unclean hands. He
would point out that contrary to the case of the petitioner that he joined on
the basis of the joining report when the petitioner came forth with the
order he was issued with the order dated 17.09.2013, English translation
of which is as follows:
 "Ref: UEPPCB/HO/Gen-01/2013/4733-561
Sept. 17, 2013
 To,
 Dr. T.B. Singh,
 Senior Scientific Officer,
 Himanchal State Pollution Control Board
 Regional Laboratory,
 PONTA SAAHIB (Himanchal Pradesh)
 Subject: Your letter dated 16.09.2013 regarding joining on the post
 of Chief Environment Officer at Uttarakhand Environment
 Protection and Pollution Control Board.
 Sir,
 Please refer your letter dated 16.09.2013 submitted to this office
on the subject matter cited above. In this regard, it is to inform you that
as per Uttar Pradesh Pollution Control Board Service Regulation 1995,
the Chairman of the Uttarakhand Environment Protection and Pollution
Control Board is the appointing authority of the Chief Environment
Officer. Sine no formal appointment order has been issued by the
Competent Authority for your appointment, therefore, in such
circumstances, it is not possible to accept your letter by this office.
Hence, your letter submitted to this office is not accepted and returned in
original.
Enclosed: As above.
 Faithfully,
 --Sd--
 Date: 17.09.2013
 (Vinod Singhal)
 Member Secretary
16. The case of the petitioner is based on Annexure-9 dated
10.09.2013. Even, according to the petitioner's own pleading, it is issued
by the Additional Secretary of the Government of Uttarakhand. Translated
version of the order dated 10.09.2013 is as follows:
 "No.894/X-3-13-13(09)2006
From,
 Manoj Chandran

8
 Additional Secretary
 Government of Uttarakhand
 To,
 Member Secretary
 Uttarakhand Environment Protection and Pollution Control
 Board, Dehradun.
 Forest and Environment Section-3 Dehradun dated 10th Sep. 2013
Subject:Regarding deputation of Dr. T.B. Singh, Senior Scientific
Officer, Himachal Pradesh Pollution Control Board, Shimla on
the post of Chief Environment Officer.
 Sir,
 In the above mentioned matter after due consideration, the
Government has taken a decision that Dr. T.B. Singh, Senior Scientific
Officer, Himachal Pollution Control Board, Shimla be posted on
deputation for a period of one year on the post of Chief Environment
Officer, Uttarakhand, Environment Protection and Pollution Control
Board.

2. Therefore, in this regard, I have been directed to state that Dr.
T.B. Singh be appointed immediately and the Government be apprised of
the compliance report and joining.
 Yours truly,

Sd/-
 (Manoj Chandran)
 Additional Secretary
No. /X-3-13-13(09) 2006 Ad dated above.
CC: To the following for information and necessary action.
1. Chairman, Uttarakhand Environment Protection and Pollution Control
Board.
 2. Principal Secretary, Hon'ble Chief Minister, Government of
Uttarakhand.
 3. Member Secretary, Himachal Pradesh Pollution Control Board,
Shimla.
4. Dr. T.B. Singh, Senior Scientific Officer, Himachal Pradesh Pollution
Control Board, Shimla through Member Secretary, Himachal Pradesh
Pollution Control Board, Shimla

By order,
 Sd/-
 (Manoj Chandran)
 Additional Secretary"
17. Thereafter, it is that the impugned order is passed. Translated
version of the impugned order reads as follows:
"From,
 Manoj Chandran,
 Additional Secretary,
 Government of Uttarakhand.

9
To,
 Member Secretary,
 Uttarakhand Environment Protection and Pollution Control
 Board, Dehradun.
 Forest and Environment Section-3 Dehradun dated: 17th Sept, 2013.
 Subject: Regarding deputation of Dr. T.B. Singh, Senior Scientific
 Officer, Himanchal Pradesh Pollution Control Board,
 Shimla on the post of Chief Environment Officer.
 Sir,
 In reference to the aforesaid matter, kindly refer the Government
Order No. 894/X-3-13-13 (09) 2006 dated 10th September, 2013 with the
above subject by which the decision was taken to post Dr. T.B. Singh
Senior Scientific Officer, Himanchal Pradesh Pollution Control Board,
Shimla as Chief Environmental Officer at Uttarakhand Environment
Protection and Pollution Control Board on deputation for a period of one
year.
 2. In this regard, I have been directed to say that the above order is
stayed. Kindly, therefore take necessary action in this regard,
accordingly.
 Yours truly,
 Sd/-
 (Manoj Chandran)

18. At the time, when the interim order was passed, it was not brought
to the notice of the Court. Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner
would, in reply, point out that as regards the complaints against him, there
is no enquiry contemplated under Article 311 of the Constitution and he
would submit that it is only that he had taken action against some persons
that complaints came against him. He would also submit that the order
dated 17.09.2013, which is relied on by the learned counsel for the Board,
was not served on him.
19. Going by the Regulations made in the year 1995 in the State of
Uttar Pradesh and which has been adopted in the State of Uttarakhand
also, the post of Chief Environment Officer, shown to exist in nine
temporary posts, is to be filled up 50 per cent by promotion from amongst
technical officers and the person has to be designated as Chief
Environment Officer (Engineer). Further 50 per cent is to be promoted
again by promotion from amongst substantively appointed Scientific
Officers. There are various other requirements, which we are not dilating
on. The persons, so appointed, are designated as Chief Environment
Officer (Scientist). In the Rules, under the heading 'Source of

10
Recruitment' it is also mentioned that if there is any shortfall from
amongst the Technical Officer or Scientific Officer, the post can be filled
up from other category, so much so that, the vacancy so filled will be
considered in the next recruitment and the quota will be raised.
Therefore, there are elaborate provisions made in the matter of
appointment for the post of Chief Environment Officer and the
Appointing Authority is shown as the Chairman. Therefore, it is quite
clear that the Additional Secretary or anyone else in the Government has
no role whatsoever in the appointment to the post of Chief Environment
Officer. Met with this situation, the contention of the petitioner would
appear to be that since the Chairperson is also the Principal Secretary and
going by Notings in the File which we have adverted to at the behest of
the Chief Minister, he has passed an order for appointment that will serve
as an appointment order. On the other hand, the case of the respondent is
that the Chairperson as such has not issued an order. Even going by
Annexure 9, it is an order issued by the Additional Secretary of the
Government. Going by the tenor of the order, it is an order issued by the
Government, therefore, it cannot be treated to be an order issued by the
Chairperson under the Regulations. We would think, in the facts of this
case, reminding ourselves that this is a discretionary jurisdiction, we
cannot for a moment accept the case of the petitioner. The petitioner is,
undoubtedly, an officer, who was borne in the cadre of the Himanchal
Pradesh State Pollution Control Board. He may have served in one
instance as Chief Environment Officer earlier, this is a case, where we
keep in mind the submission of the learned Advocate General that even if
it is by deputation, there must be some method. Here, the petitioner has
apparently moved the Authorities and he has been appointed on
deputation. The appointment is, as already noticed, going by what is
issued to him, issued by a totally incompetent person, namely, the
Additional Secretary in the Government. It may be true that going by the
Notings, it is at the behest of the then Chief Minister, that the Principal
Secretary has passed an order, namely, to appoint him. We will proceed
to think that the Principal Secretary is also the Chairperson, but when
again the then Chief Minister has directed the matter to be kept in

11
suspension as evident from the Notings at the very next page at Page 443
and directed the earlier order to be kept in abeyance, the letter was issued.
The appointment of the petitioner is premised on a thoroughly precarious
basis; he seeks appointment to a post by deputation; he is given
appointment by deputation in the manner, which we have already referred
to. The Rules, which have been adopted, clearly provide for appointment
by way of promotion. The argument based on the 2006 Regulations, on
the face of it, is unacceptable as the learned Senior Counsel for the
petitioner fairly submits that the said Rules have not been published in the
gazette. A perusal of the said Rules, which the petitioner sought to draw
support from, categorically states that the Regulations will come into
force on the day it is published in the gazette. Learned Senior Counsel
for the petitioner does not have a case that the Regulations contemplated
under Section 14(4) are not subordinate legislation. The Board, which
made the Regulations, also intended the Regulations to come into force
only after they are published in the gazette. It may be true that there is a
difference in the matter of making Regulations in the Water Act and in the
AIR Act. Whatever that be, in view of the fact that the Regulations,
which have been made in the year 2006, have not come into force,
petitioner cannot lay store by the said Regulations. Then, the only
argument of the petitioner would appear to be based on the resolution of
the Board and the effect of Section 21 of the General Clauses Act.
Section 21 of the General Clauses Act only enables a body making the
law (subordinate legislation) to vary or amend the same. By no stretch of
imagination, can we take the view that the decision taken by the Board to
fill up the vacant post by direct recruitment on deputation to be an
amendment of the extant Regulations. We are of the view, however, that
we need not premise the rejection of the petitioner's claim on the said
basis as we take the view at any rate that it cannot be said in this case that
the petitioner has been issued an order of appointment by the Chairman as
such. If the petitioner lays store by Annexure-9, even, according to his
own showing, it is only an order issued by the Additional Secretary of the
Government. We would think that in the facts of this case, no ground at
all is made out for granting any relief to the petitioner.

12
20. In the circumstances, we see no merit in the case. The writ petition
stands dismissed.
(V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C. J.)
 09.09.2014 09.09.2014
Arpan
